units.source_text: 过去我常常产生一种奇妙的想法，却从不曾把金阁和空袭联系起来。

en.t: In the past I often had a strange thought, yet I had never connected the Golden Pavilion with air raids.

units.source_text: 塞班岛沦陷以后，本土遭受空袭在所难免。

en.t: After Saipan fell, it became inevitable that the homeland would suffer air raids.

units.source_text: 京都市部分地区迅速强制疏散。

en.t: Parts of Kyoto City were quickly subjected to forced evacuation.

units.source_text: 尽管如此，金阁这个半永恒的存在和空袭的灾难，在我心中只能是彼此无缘的东西。

en.t: Even so, in my mind the half-eternal existence of the Golden Pavilion and the disaster of air raids could only be things unrelated to each other.

units.source_text: 我深知金刚不坏的金阁，与那科学上的火相互间是截然不同性质的东西，它们一相遇，仿佛就会迅速相互躲闪似的……

en.t: I knew deeply that the indestructible Golden Pavilion and that scientific fire were things of utterly different natures, as though the moment they met they would swiftly dodge away from each other...

units.source_text: 可是，过不多久，金阁也许会毁于空袭的战火。

en.t: And yet, before long, the Golden Pavilion might be destroyed in the flames of an air raid.

units.source_text: 照这样下去，金阁化为灰烬将是确实无疑的。

en.t: At this rate, it was certain beyond doubt that the Golden Pavilion would be reduced to ashes.
